analysis.title: Europe Open - Jury's still out
key_insights: Nvidia shares traded slightly stronger after earnings reiterated a strong demand outlook and sales, but doubts remain on leadership as the board confirmed Jensen Huang will not return as CEO.
Citi Research's Nvidia first take: demand remains very strong, supply constraints are easing, and interim management raised long-term growth expectations.
Nvidia's more selective approach to financing AI infrastructure projects could moderate growth for some neocloud operators if funding becomes constrained.
Asian equities were mixed: Kospi and Nikkei modestly higher, the rest of the region lower. US equity futures drifted higher (Nasdaq +0.5%) and USTs were slightly stronger.

Fed speakers continue to downplay the need for a 50bp hike. Williams said there was no need for a 'dramatic' move and Hammack preferred slow and steady hikes. Musalem (non-voter) saw 'several' hikes before Spring.

UK October CPI matched consensus, but services (3.7% YoY) and headline (3.6% YoY) were below MPC expectations. December OIS pricing remains tilted toward a hike at about 17bp, down from highs near 20bp after the labor data.

Australia Q3 wage price index rose 1.1% QoQ, the strongest quarterly gain in 3 years and above the 1% consensus. Citi economists expect wage growth to overshoot RBA forecasts, and a beat on tomorrow's employment data could mean further tightening.

G10 FX traded in extremely tight ranges against the USD, with interbank volumes about 14% below 30-day averages. AUD options saw selling interest, with the 3m 25d risk reversal at 1.3 vols in favor of AUD puts.

Gold fell nearly 2% overnight and broke the $3,800 handle with no clear driver beyond falling oil and lower yields. It is on track for its worst annual performance since 2013 (-12% YTD), and the move is being characterized as a potential capitulation.
ECB succession reports: de Cos is said to be the sole contender for ECB President, and Germany is said to be set to propose Markus Brunnermeier as ECB chief economist.
RBNZ: recent employment data suggests the hiking cycle is likely over. Citi expects the OCR to hold at 2.75% throughout 2027.
